method: Viewed every individual motion PNG, in numeric order within each scene and profile.

findings.movement: Camera follows the ringed aircraft as it banks off the coast and past the fleet. Other aircraft change position and heading, and vessels progress through the frame; the ring stays centered on the player in these samples.
findings.wakes: Carrier and escort wakes stay connected at visible sterns and aligned to vessel headings. The long diffuse plumes could use more water texture.
findings.coastline: The sand and shallows hold together as the runway scrolls. White foam strokes evolve along the coast but remain visibly separated from the wet-sand boundary in places.
findings.impacts: Hull reads 35% at 000 and 27% at 006. The white damage flash and small orange impact are visible by 006, and ordinary aircraft shading returns by 024. At 060 a larger orange burst is easy to separate from the paired tracers; smoke and sparse embers persist at 090 and thin out later.
findings.consistency: Both profiles show the same sequence and placement. The fallback loses edge detail, and the Hawk label crosses the objective banner in the last coast frame. I saw no blocking disappearance, detached ship wake, or discontinuous coastline among the sampled frames.

limits: These 36 sampled stills cover visible progression only. They do not establish continuous smoothness, frame pacing, device performance, or parity with a separately rendered motion control.
